components.note: 可 (kě) appears twice, stacked; the doubled shape is also where the sound gē comes from

example.english: My older brother works in Beijing.
example.fact: 哥 on its own is mostly a term of address ("Big Brother"), while the family term is the doubled 哥哥. Friendly speech stretches it: 大哥 for any respected older man, and 哥们儿 for a buddy, especially in northern speech.

components.note: Simplified form of 類; the 米 over 大 shape is a simplification, not a picture of rice or bigness

example.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan nǎ yí lèi diànyǐng?
example.english: What kind of movies do you like?
example.fact: 类 groups things into broad categories and works like a measure word in 这类人 or 一类问题. Compare 种 (zhǒng), which stresses a specific variety; 类 sits a level above it, as in 分类 (to classify) and 种类 (kinds).

components.note: 王 (jade) — 瑞 originally meant a jade token, and jade stands for something precious and fortunate
耑 (duān) gives only a faint sound hint for ruì

example.english: A timely snow foretells a good harvest year.
example.fact: 瑞 is almost always bound inside words and sayings. 瑞雪 (timely snow) is a winter blessing for farmers because snow cover protects wheat, which is why the proverb ties it to a bumper year. It also appears in country names like 瑞士 (Switzerland) and 瑞典 (Sweden).

components.note: 尸 (body) — the human body here
水 (water) — liquid leaving the body

example.english: The baby wet the bed.
example.fact: 尿 is both noun and verb: 尿尿 is the childlike word, 撒尿 is blunt, and 小便 is the polite register. Its measure word is 泡 (pāo), as in 一泡尿. In some northern speech the noun is read suī instead of niào.

components.note: 尸 (body) — something coming out of the body
米 (rice) — hints at food passing through the body

example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu zài yuànzi lǐ lā shǐ le.
example.english: The puppy pooped in the yard.
example.fact: 屎 is crude, and the verb phrase is 拉屎 (literally "pull poop"); polite speech uses 大便. The character also shows up in harmless compounds like 眼屎 (eye gunk) and 耳屎 (earwax).

components.note: 木 (wood) — the old sense was a wooden frame or branch, hence grids and standards
各 (gè) gives the sound; same syllable, different tone

example.hanzi: 请在表格里写你的名字。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài biǎogé lǐ xiě nǐ de míngzi.
example.english: Please write your name in the table.
example.fact: 格 is mostly a building block of compounds: 表格 (form), 价格 (price), 性格 (personality), 资格 (qualification). The idea behind them all is a fixed frame that something must fit into. It also names the boxes of a grid: 一格 is one square or one bar of signal.

components.note: Began as a drawing of a left hand; the 工 was added later and the hand shape became the top stroke

example.english: Please turn left.
example.fact: 左右 is both the pair "left and right" and, after a number, "approximately": 三十岁左右 means around thirty. In politics 左 maps onto "the Left" as in English, but in much ancient usage 右 was the side of honour.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the sea is a body of water
每 (měi) gives a rough sound hint for hǎi

example.english: We are going to the seaside this weekend.
example.fact: 海 stretches into figurative "vast sea of" phrases: 人海 (sea of people), 云海 (sea of clouds). The city 上海 literally means "on the sea". Large inland lakes can also be called 海, such as 中南海 in Beijing.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a building, here a government office, with 官 first meaning a place of official business

example.english: He wants to become an official.
example.fact: 当官 (to become an official) has a hint of ambition and sometimes irony. The same character gives 器官 (organ) and 五官 (the five facial features) because those are the body's "officers", each with a duty. 官方 means "official" in the sense of authorized.

components.note: 目 (eye) — an eye sighting along a line, so the thing seen is straight
十 (ten) — a vertical line inside the shape suggesting straightness

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù yìzhí wǎng qián zǒu.
example.english: Go straight ahead along this road.
example.fact: In 一直 the word means either "straight on" in space (一直走) or "all along, continuously" in time (他一直在等你). 直 also carries "frank": 直说 is to speak bluntly, and 直接 means direct.

components.note: Simplified form of 樂, whose old shape is usually explained as a musical instrument mounted on wood; the "music" sense is why 乐 also has a second reading

example.english: Happy birthday to you!
example.fact: 乐 is a classic two-reading character: lè means "happy" (快乐), but yuè means "music" (音乐). The meanings are connected, since music was the original source of joy. As a surname it is Yuè.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — sits below the hand stroke; the right hand is the one that brings food to the mouth

example.pinyin: Tā zuò zài wǒ de yòubian.
example.english: He sits on my right.
example.fact: In early China 右 often marked the higher rank: 右丞相 outranked 左丞相 in some dynasties, and the idiom 无出其右 means "none surpasses him". Pairing with 左 gives 左右, "about", as in 三点左右 (around three o'clock).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — lifting is done by hand
兴 (xīng) is the simplified top of 舉; it is a leftover shape, not a sound clue

example.english: Please raise your hand to answer.
example.fact: 举 extends from raising things to "citing" them: 举例 means to give an example, and 举个例子 ("raise an example") is a very common phrase. It also forms formal verbs for events, such as 举行 (to hold a ceremony) and 举办 (to organize).

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house, shelter
女 (woman) — a woman under a roof is the classic picture of calm and safety

example.english: Good night, see you tomorrow.
example.fact: 安 appears in greetings like 早安 and 晚安 and in 平安 (safe and sound). It is also a verb meaning "to install" in 安装, and the root of 安全 (safety), 安静 (quiet) and 安排 (to arrange).

components.note: Simplified form of 師; the 刂 on the left is a graphic reduction, not the knife radical in its usual meaning

example.english: My teacher is very nice.
example.fact: 师 almost never stands alone in speech. It attaches to professions: 老师 (teacher), 医师 (doctor), 律师 (lawyer), 厨师 (chef). 师傅 is a respectful address for a skilled worker, and people commonly call a taxi driver 师傅.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — falling leaves and petals are the image behind the word
洛 (luò) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Shùyè cóng shù shang luò xiàlai.
example.english: Leaves fall from the tree.
example.fact: 落 has three readings: luò (to fall), là (to be left behind, as in 落了东西, "left something behind") and lào (in 落枕, a stiff neck). The luò sense also gives 落后 (to fall behind) and 降落 (to land).

components.note: Simplified form of 錄; the original metal radical was dropped, leaving a compact shape

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè duàn huà lù xiàlai.
example.english: Please record this passage.
example.fact: 录 covers writing things down and capturing audio or video: 录音 (sound recording), 录像 (video recording), 记录 (a record). 录取 means to admit or hire, so 被录取了 is what applicants hope to hear.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — a slope
又 (hand) — a hand on a slope, usually explained as climbing back, from which "turn back, reverse" grew

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu chuān fǎn le.
example.english: This garment is on inside out.
example.fact: 反 works as a result complement meaning "the wrong way round": 穿反 (put on backwards), 放反 (put the wrong way up). It also gives 反而 ("on the contrary"), 反对 (to oppose) and 正反 (positive and negative).

components.note: 王 (jade) — 理 first meant cutting jade along its grain, the root of 'pattern, order'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound exactly

example.english: What you say makes sense.
example.fact: 理 as a verb means "to pay attention to": 他不理我 means he ignores me. As a noun it is the logic behind things (道理, 理由). 整理 means to tidy up and 理科 is the science stream at school.

components.note: Older form shows two hands (the 八 at the bottom) holding something up to offer it; 'prepare, equip' became 'tool'

example.pinyin: Zhèxiē gōngjù wǒ dōu dài lái le.
example.english: I have brought all these tools.
example.fact: 具 is a bound form in 工具 (tool), 家具 (furniture), 玩具 (toy) and 具体 (concrete, specific). In formal writing 具有 means "to possess", and 具 is also a measure word for corpses and heavy objects, as in 一具尸体.

components.note: 尸 (building) — a roofed building, in the older form a house with several levels
云 replaces 曾 of the traditional 層; it is a simplification, not a sound clue

example.english: I live on the third floor.
example.fact: 层 counts floors in mainland usage (三层, the third floor) and also layers of anything: 一层灰 (a layer of dust). Floors can also be called 楼, as in 三楼. The idiom 层出不穷 describes things that keep appearing one after another.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — digging is done by hand or hand tool
穵 (wā) is an older character for digging itself and gives the sound

example.hanzi: 他在花园里挖了一个坑。
example.pinyin: Tā zài huāyuán lǐ wā le yí ge kēng.
example.english: He dug a hole in the garden.
example.fact: 挖 works for anything dug out, from a pit to a tunnel: 挖洞, 挖土. 挖苦 is a figurative idiom meaning to mock sarcastically, and 挖墙脚 ("dig at someone's wall foot") means to poach a person or deal from someone else.

components.note: 弋 (yì) a stake or marker
工 (work) — craft and a fixed pattern to follow

example.english: I like Chinese-style dishes.
example.fact: 式 is a suffix meaning "-style": 中式, 西式, 日式. It also forms 方式 (way, manner), 正式 (formal) and 公式 (formula). Adding it to a place name is a handy way to say "in that manner", as in 美式咖啡 (Americano).

components.note: 土 (earth) — earth packed into a gap is the root idea of plugging
宀 (roof) — an enclosed space being filled

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yīfu sāi jìn bāo lǐ.
example.english: He stuffed his clothes into the bag.
example.fact: 塞 has three readings: sāi (to stuff), sè (blocked, as in 堵塞) and sài (a frontier fortress, as in 边塞). 塞车 means traffic jam, common in Taiwan and southern speech, whereas mainland usage prefers 堵车.

components.note: The oldest shape is debated (often linked to a tool or a boat); the modern meanings are square, side, direction

example.english: Where do you live?
example.fact: 方 covers geometry (平方米, square metre) and the "side" in 对方 (the other party) or 双方 (both sides). Note that 地方 with a neutral second syllable (dìfang) means "place", while dìfāng with a full tone means "local, regional".

meanings: to carry on a shoulder pole

components.note: 扌 (hand) — picking out with the hand
兆 (zhào) gives a loose sound clue for tiāo

example.pinyin: Nǐ bāng wǒ tiāo yí jiàn yīfu ba.
example.english: Help me pick out a piece of clothing.
example.fact: 挑 has two readings: tiāo (to choose, to carry on a pole) and tiǎo (to poke or provoke, as in 挑战, challenge). 挑食 means to be a picky eater and 挑剔 means to be fussy about details.

components.note: 辛 (xīn) means acrid or hot-tasting, matching the burning taste
束 (shù) gives a faint sound clue for là

example.hanzi: 这个菜太辣了，我吃不了。
example.pinyin: Zhège cài tài là le, wǒ chī bu liǎo.
example.english: This dish is too spicy, I can't eat it.
example.fact: 辣 describes chilli heat, and 麻辣 combines it with the numbing tingle (麻) of Sichuan pepper, a very Sichuan flavour pairing. It also describes stinging pain, as in 火辣辣 (burning hot), and 辣妹 is a "spicy girl" in slang.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting is done with a blade
七 (qī) gives the sound; qiē is a close match

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ píngguǒ qiē chéng xiǎo kuài.
example.english: Please cut the apple into small pieces.
example.fact: 切 has two readings: qiē (to cut) and qiè (close, earnest, as in 亲切 and 密切). The word 一切 ("everything") uses qiè, a typical learner trap.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — beckoning is a hand gesture
召 (zhào) gives the sound, and also means to summon

example.english: He waved at me.
example.fact: 招手 is more general than English "wave": it covers beckoning, hailing a taxi, and waving hello. As a noun 招 means a move or trick (高招, a clever move), and 招聘 means to recruit staff.

components.note: 火 (fire) — explosions involve fire
乍 (zhà) gives the sound exactly

example.english: The balloon burst.
example.fact: 炸 has two readings: zhà (to explode) and zhá (to deep-fry, as in 炸鸡). 炸弹 is a bomb, and in slang 炸了 can mean someone is furious, a place is chaotic, or something is amazing.

components.note: 土 (earth) — walls were built of rammed earth
啬 (sè) is left over from traditional 牆; the sound link is weak now

example.pinyin: Qiáng shang guà zhe yì fú huà.
example.english: A painting hangs on the wall.
example.fact: The measure word depends on the wall: 一面墙 for a surface and 一堵墙 for a standing barrier. The proverb 隔墙有耳 ("walls have ears") warns that secrets can be overheard.

components.note: 氵 (water) — flowing is what water does
㐬 (liú) gives the sound exactly

example.english: The river flows east.
example.fact: 流 extends from water to anything that moves smoothly: 流利 (fluent), 流行 (fashionable, spreading like a current) and 交流 (to exchange). 流泪 means to shed tears and 流血 means to bleed.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — putting something up by hand
荅 (dá) gives the sound; dā is a near match

example.english: We are taking the train to Shanghai.
example.fact: 搭 means to catch a ride: 搭火车, 搭飞机; in mainland usage 坐 is more common for "to ride". It also means to pair things up: 搭配 (to match, as clothes or food) and 搭档 (a partner).

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree being looked at
目 (eye) — an eye examining; the standard explanation of "to look at", later "mutual"

example.english: We should help each other.
example.fact: 相 as xiāng is an adverb meaning "mutually" in 相信, 相爱, 相同. As xiàng it means appearance or photograph: 照相 (to take a photo), 相片. Same character, different tone, different meaning.

components.note: 木 (wood) — the old character 權 was a tree and also a balance weight
又 stands in for the complex right half of 權 in the simplified form

example.hanzi: 每个人都有说话的权利。
example.pinyin: Měi ge rén dōu yǒu shuōhuà de quánlì.
example.english: Everyone has the right to speak.
example.fact: 权利 (right, entitlement) and 权力 (power, authority) are both pronounced quánlì, which makes them an easy pair to confuse in listening. 权 also appears in 人权 (human rights), 版权 (copyright) and 权威 (authority).

components.note: 羽 (feather) — wings flapping and turning over
番 (fān) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fān dào dì shí yè.
example.english: Please turn to page ten of the book.
example.fact: 翻 is to flip or turn over, as in 翻页 (turn a page) and 翻身 (turn over in bed). 翻译 (to translate) literally means turning one language over to another, and 翻脸 means to suddenly turn hostile.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — arranging things by hand
罢 (bà) gives the sound; bǎi is close

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang bǎi zhe hěn duō shuǐguǒ.
example.english: Lots of fruit is laid out on the table.
example.fact: 摆 suggests putting things out in an orderly or visible way: 摆摊 (set up a stall), 摆桌子 (to lay a table). 摆手 means waving the hand, which in China often means "no" or "stop"; 摆脱 means to shake off.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — an overhang above
土 (earth) — earth pressing down under it, the picture behind 'press'

example.english: He is under a lot of pressure.
example.fact: 压力 means both physical pressure and mental stress. 压岁钱 is the red-envelope money given to children at the New Year. 血压 is blood pressure, and the colloquial 压根儿 (yàgēnr) means "at all" in negative statements.

components.note: 火 (fire) — roasting needs fire
考 (kǎo) gives the sound exactly

example.english: Let's grill fish this evening.
example.fact: 烤 is used for roasting, baking and barbecuing, so 烤鸭 is roast duck, 烤箱 is an oven and 烤火 means to warm oneself by a fire. 烤 can also describe burning in the sun: 被太阳烤着.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — a cliff face where water comes out
泉 (quán) — a spring; the old meaning of 原 was 'source', and the sound link is faint

example.english: So it was you!
example.fact: 原来 can mean "originally" or "so it turns out" in a realization like 原来是你. 原 is the older form of 源 (source) and also appears in 原因 (reason), 原谅 (to forgive) and 草原 (grassland).

components.note: 火 (fire) — a light source
丁 (dīng) gives a faint sound clue for dēng

example.english: Please turn off the light.
example.fact: 灯 has the measure word 盏: 一盏灯. 开灯 and 关灯 are "turn on / off the light". 红绿灯 is the traffic light, and the Lantern Festival (元宵节) is also called 灯节.

components.note: Its origin is debated; in modern use it mostly appears in words as a sound or suffix, as in 尾巴

example.english: I can't wait to get home.
example.fact: 巴不得 is a fixed phrase meaning "to be dying to", and it is used for things the speaker eagerly wants. Elsewhere 巴 serves as a soft suffix in 嘴巴 (mouth) and 尾巴 (tail), and as the transliteration in 巴士 (bus).

components.note: 禾 (grain) — the tip of a stalk, from which 'small, slight' developed
肖 (xiāo) gives the sound; shāo is a near match

example.english: Please wait a moment.
example.fact: 稍 is an adverb that needs a verb or adjective: 稍大 (slightly larger), 稍等 (wait a moment). 请稍等 is the standard service phrase, and the fuller 稍微 means the same thing.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 僅 started with a person radical
又 stands in for the complex right half of traditional 僅

example.hanzi: 他仅用了十分钟就做完了。
example.pinyin: Tā jǐn yòng le shí fēnzhōng jiù zuò wán le.
example.english: He finished in only ten minutes.
example.fact: 仅 is the more formal, written counterpart of 只: 不仅...而且 (not only ... but also) and 仅仅 (just, merely) are common. It is pronounced like 尽 in some uses, which is a source of confusion.

components.note: 纟 (silk) — tying and knots were done with thread
吉 (jí) gives the sound; jié is close

example.english: They got married last year.
example.fact: 结 is read jié (to tie, to conclude: 结婚, 结束) and jiē (to bear fruit). 结果 is jiéguǒ meaning "result" but jiēguǒ meaning "bear fruit", a famous minimal pair. Its noun sense is a knot: 打结.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pulling is done by hand
止 (zhǐ) gives only a weak sound hint for chě

example.english: Don't pull on my clothes.
example.fact: 扯 starts as a physical pull, then becomes colloquial for rambling: 瞎扯 (talk nonsense), 闲扯 (chat idly), 扯淡 (rubbish, crude). 扯后腿 means to hold someone back.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — the indigo plant, source of the dye
监 (jiān) gives only a loose sound hint for lán

example.english: The sky is blue.
example.fact: 蓝 first named the indigo plant. The classic saying 青出于蓝而胜于蓝 means the dye outshines the plant, so a student can surpass the teacher. 蓝牙 is Bluetooth and 蓝领 is blue-collar.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a mould shaped from clay
刑 (xíng) gives the sound exactly

example.english: What is your blood type?
example.fact: 型 is mainly a suffix: 血型 (blood type), 发型 (hairstyle), 脸型 (face shape), 大型 (large-scale), 型号 (model number). Its original sense was a casting mould.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — shouting uses the mouth
内 (nèi) gives a rough sound hint for nà

example.english: He shouted loudly.
example.fact: 呐 is used almost only in 呐喊 (to cry out, rally). Lu Xun's first short-story collection is 《呐喊》 (1923), which made the word widely known. As a sentence particle people more often write 哪 or 呢.

excludeSuggestion: Bound character, appearing almost only in 呐喊

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the hand component
卩 (kneeling person) and 又 (hand): the right half is often explained as a person being seized, later 'to give a report/verdict'

example.english: I read the newspaper every morning.
example.fact: 报 covers announcing (报告, 报名 to sign up, 报警 to call the police) and a newspaper (看报, 报纸). It also means "to repay": 报答 is to repay a kindness, and 报仇 is to take revenge.
